heading: INT. FAMILY MINIVAN, DRIVE-THRU CAR WASH - DAY

units.text: INT. FAMILY MINIVAN, DRIVE-THRU CAR WASH - DAY
Soap foam crawls across the windshield.
Brushes thump and swish.
Inside, the world is a muffled aquarium.
LORETTA PEMBERTON-SHAH (40s, driver, rings clacking against the wheel) keeps both hands at ten and two.
In the passenger seat sits her father, HAROLD PEMBERTON (70s, flat cap, silent for forty miles).
In the back, her daughter ZINNIA (14, earbuds in, knees up) watches the brushes beat the glass.
The conveyor tugs the van forward.
A giant mitt of foam slaps the roof.
You didn't have to come.
units.name: LORETTA

units.text: I wanted to.
units.name: HAROLD

units.text: You hate car washes.
units.name: LORETTA

units.text: I hate being left behind more.
units.name: HAROLD

units.text: Zinnia pulls out one earbud.
Who left who?
units.name: ZINNIA

units.text: Loretta and Harold look at each other.
Neither speaks.
The brushes whump against the doors.
^Nobody left anybody.
units.name: LORETTA

units.text: ^Nobody left anybody.
units.name: HAROLD

units.text: Zinnia raises both eyebrows and puts the earbud back.
The conveyor slows.
A rinse arch sprays them white.
In the sudden silence, Loretta lets go of the wheel for the first time all day and presses her fingers into her eyes.
Harold reaches over and, with enormous awkwardness, pats her knee twice.
Your mother liked this part.
units.name: HAROLD

units.text: The foam.
units.name: LORETTA

units.text: The foam.
units.name: HAROLD

units.text: The dryers blast.
Zinnia leans forward between the seats and rests her chin on the headrest, close to both of them.
Sunlight breaks through the last of the water.
Loretta turns on the wipers.
